assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Make a complete game sprite atlas for Giuseppe Garibaldi as a friendly ghost in an existing southern Brazilian pixel-art RPG. Image 1 (Anita sheet) is the STRICT style and proportions reference: same chunky outlined 3.5-head-tall body, large expressive head, crisp visible pixel clusters, warm shading, NOT painterly realistic. Image 2 (old Garibaldi) establishes ONLY identity: middle aged Italian man with brown wavy hair and full brown beard, dark navy beret, RED rolled-sleeve shirt, black neckerchief, striped brown gaucho poncho over one shoulder, wide belt, loose brown-gray bombachas, brown boots. Render his entire body opaque with a subtle pale blue rim, NO fog or glow clouds; engine handles ghost translucency. EXACT 4 columns x 3 rows, 12 separate full-body poses on genuinely transparent background. Generous empty gutters and margins, identical body and head scale and aligned feet in each cell. Row1 front: [neutral idle, left leg forward walk, passing stride, right leg forward walk]. Row2 facing RIGHT profile: [idle, left leg forward, passing stride, right leg forward]. Row3: [back idle, back left-leg-forward, back right-leg-forward, friendly speaking gesture with right hand raised facing right]. Clear alternating articulated legs. Character ONLY, no weapons held, no environment, no text, no labels, no grid, no shadows on ground. Same clothes/identity in all12 poses. Match Anita art faithfully.

Edit this ship background sprite. KEEP its exact crisp pixel-art materials, warm wood, ornate dark hull and brass lanterns, stern on left and bow on right, no masts or objects added. Change ONLY the deck's playable depth and framing: make the open floor vertically about 55% deeper, with more parallel plank rows, while keeping its overall horizontal width. Output2048x1024. The outline stays horizontal: flat stern left, rounded pointed bow right. The back rail is around y130 and playable floor begins around y215; at center x1000 the floor extends down to y730, near/front rail around y750 and visible hull side ends around y880. At far right bow the point is near(1980,490). Aim for wide usable floor for combat, not a thin side view. Keep a continuous empty central floor. Fully transparent outside the ship, generous margin, no water/sea, no floor shadows or glow clouds, no characters, no hatches, no barrels, no cannons or poles. Preserve the drawing quality and same wood, do not merely stretch all pixels; draw the deeper floor and matching hull perspective.

Use case: stylized-concept. Transparent sprite atlas for same richly crafted earthy pixel-art RPG style as reference1, 40-degree elevated view, warm timber, worn cream canvas and iron. EXACT 4 columns x 2 rows, 8 isolated DIFFERENT assets, generous gutters, each wholly separated. Row1 left to right: [one tall full wooden sail mast with two spread yards and two weathered patched cream square sails, narrow rigging, broad wooden mast footing, no flag; a second distinct tall mast with one furled upper sail and a partially torn lower cream sail, no flag; one upright timber barrel with dark iron bands; rectangular wooden ship hatch with dark iron grate seen in elevated perspective]. Row2: [one small 1830s naval cannon on wooden carriage facing diagonally UP away from viewer (back of carriage in front), full shape; a sturdy boarding ladder seen from elevated front, 6 wooden rungs and hemp side ropes; a vertical naval flagpole with dark green flag and yellow diamond with tiny IMPERIAL crown/shield emblem, NOT modern Brazilian blue globe; a ship steering wheel attached to a short wooden pedestal with a small coil of rope at its foot]. All exactly same camera, pixel rendering and world, opaque objects on true transparent alpha, no backdrop, no cast shadows, no labels, no modern objects, no people. Every object entirely in own cell, masts are tall slim, smaller objects centered in own cells. Output1536x1024.

Use case: stylized-concept. One complete small southern Brazilian 1830s wooden lanchão Seival boat sprite, elevated top-down 3/4 RPG view, long axis horizontal, stern LEFT and tapered bow RIGHT, no diagonal isometric tilt. Same crisp detailed warm pixel-art rendering as reference interior: strong dark outlines, woodgrain pixel clusters, warm amber timber and muted colors. Broad EMPTY open deck and low seats so THREE game characters can stand inside; perspective shows interior of hull. Dark lower hull and fine golden-brown rails. A SMALL brass/iron cannon on a wooden mounting at the far RIGHT bow facing diagonally upward, tiny wooden rudder at far LEFT stern, coiled rope tucked side. NO big sails/mast to hide the characters, NO people, no sea, no ground shadow, no background, no text or flags. Genuine transparent background. Whole boat centered with wide gutters, width roughly three times height, detailed enough for 430px-wide in-game rendering. Friendly stylized adventure game, not photoreal.

Use case: stylized-concept. Seamless TOP-DOWN dark teal blue coastal water tile for a richly illustrated pixel-art 2D RPG, night sea around a ghost sailing ship. Entire image square1024x1024 covered in water. Calm subtle irregular overlapping ripples, muted blue/teal green, very sparse thin desaturated silver flecks, gentle low contrast so characters and attacks on ship remain readable. Crisp pixel clusters, consistent small pixel scale, NOT photo, not brush painting, no large foam stripes, no objects, no coastline, no shore, no sky, no horizon, no text. Seamless repeating texture edges. Rich depth with restrained palette, natural appealing stylized game water.
